units.text: Below is a summary of all of the options that GNU ⟦0⟧ accepts. Multiple single letter options (unless they take an argument) can be combined into a single command line argument.
units.sourceHTML: Below is a summary of all of the options that GNU diff3 accepts. Multiple single letter options (unless they take an argument) can be combined into a single command line argument.

units.text: Treat all files as text and compare them line-by-line, even if they do not appear to be text. See ⟦0⟧Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Treat all files as text and compare them line-by-line, even if they do not appear to be text. See Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons.

units.text: Incorporate all unmerged changes from ⟦0⟧ to ⟦1⟧ into ⟦2⟧, surrounding conflicts with bracket lines. See ⟦3⟧Marking Conflicts⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Incorporate all unmerged changes from older to yours into mine, surrounding conflicts with bracket lines. See Marking Conflicts.

units.text: Use the compatible comparison program ⟦0⟧ to compare files instead of ⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use the compatible comparison program program to compare files instead of diff.

units.text: Generate an ⟦0⟧ script that incorporates all the changes from ⟦1⟧ to ⟦2⟧ into ⟦3⟧. See ⟦4⟧Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate⟦5⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Generate an ed script that incorporates all the changes from older to yours into mine. See Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate.

units.text: Like ⟦0⟧, except bracket lines from overlapping changes’ first and third files. See ⟦1⟧Marking Conflicts⟦2⟧. With ⟦3⟧, an overlapping change looks like this:
units.sourceHTML: Like -e, except bracket lines from overlapping changes’ first and third files. See Marking Conflicts. With -E, an overlapping change looks like this:

units.text: Output a summary of usage and then exit.
units.sourceHTML: Output a summary of usage and then exit.

units.text: Generate ‘⟦0⟧’ and ‘⟦1⟧’ commands at the end of the ⟦2⟧ script for System V compatibility. This option must be combined with one of the ⟦3⟧ options, and may not be combined with ⟦4⟧. See ⟦5⟧Saving the Changed File⟦6⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Generate ‘w’ and ‘q’ commands at the end of the ed script for System V compatibility. This option must be combined with one of the -AeExX3 options, and may not be combined with -m. See Saving the Changed File.

units.text: Use the label ⟦0⟧ for the brackets output by the ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ options. This option may be given up to three times, one for each input file. The default labels are the names of the input files. Thus ‘⟦4⟧’ acts like ‘⟦5⟧’, except that the output looks like it came from files named ‘⟦6⟧’, ‘⟦7⟧’ and ‘⟦8⟧’ rather than from files named ‘⟦9⟧’, ‘⟦10⟧’ and ‘⟦11⟧’. See ⟦12⟧Marking Conflicts⟦13⟧.

tokens.⟦4⟧:
<samp class="samp">diff3 --label X --label Y --label Z -m A
B C</samp>

units.sourceHTML: Use the label label for the brackets output by the -A, -E and -X options. This option may be given up to three times, one for each input file. The default labels are the names of the input files. Thus ‘diff3 --label X --label Y --label Z -m A B C’ acts like ‘diff3 -m A B C’, except that the output looks like it came from files named ‘X’, ‘Y’ and ‘Z’ rather than from files named ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’. See Marking Conflicts.

units.text: Apply the edit script to the first file and send the result to standard output. Unlike piping the output from ⟦0⟧ to ⟦1⟧, this works even for binary files and incomplete lines. ⟦2⟧ is assumed if no edit script option is specified. See ⟦3⟧Generating the Merged Output Directly⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Apply the edit script to the first file and send the result to standard output. Unlike piping the output from diff3 to ed, this works even for binary files and incomplete lines. -A is assumed if no edit script option is specified. See Generating the Merged Output Directly.

units.text: Strip any trailing carriage return at the end of an input line. See ⟦0⟧Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Strip any trailing carriage return at the end of an input line. See Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons.

units.text: Output a tab rather than two spaces before the text of a line in normal format. This causes the alignment of tabs in the line to look normal. See ⟦0⟧Preserving Tab Stop Alignment⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Output a tab rather than two spaces before the text of a line in normal format. This causes the alignment of tabs in the line to look normal. See Preserving Tab Stop Alignment.

units.text: Output version information and then exit.
Like ⟦0⟧, except output only the overlapping changes. See ⟦1⟧Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Like -e, except output only the overlapping changes. See Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate.

units.text: Like ⟦0⟧, except output only the overlapping changes. In other words, like ⟦1⟧, except bracket changes as in ⟦2⟧. See ⟦3⟧Marking Conflicts⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Like -E, except output only the overlapping changes. In other words, like -x, except bracket changes as in -E. See Marking Conflicts.

units.text: Like ⟦0⟧, except output only the nonoverlapping changes. See ⟦1⟧Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Like -e, except output only the nonoverlapping changes. See Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate.
